title: The Gate, and the Race Reopened

scenes.tts: The axon has been chosen. What keeps dendrite proteins from wandering into it?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Gate, and the Race Reopened. Green protein icons drift toward the start of the gold axon.
scenes.narration: The axon has been chosen. What keeps dendrite proteins from wandering into it?

scenes.tts: The first few tens of micrometres of the axon form the axon initial segment.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the proximal axon; a collar appears. Label: axon initial segment.
scenes.narration: The first few tens of micrometres of the axon form the axon initial segment.

scenes.tts: Under its membrane sits a dense coat, built on a scaffold called ankyrin G.
scenes.visual: Cutaway of the membrane: a dense coat beneath it. Label: ankyrin G.
scenes.narration: Under its membrane sits a dense coat, built on a scaffold called ankyrin G.

scenes.tts: Ankyrin G binds beta four spectrin, which links it to rings of actin under the membrane.
scenes.caption: Ankyrin G binds beta-IV spectrin, which links it to rings of actin under the membrane.
scenes.visual: Beta-IV spectrin rods link ankyrin G to periodic actin rings.
scenes.narration: Ankyrin G binds beta-IV spectrin, which links it to rings of actin under the membrane.

scenes.tts: Through its ankyrin repeats, it also binds sodium channels, K C N Q potassium channels and neurofascin one eighty-six.
scenes.caption: Through its ANK repeats, it also binds sodium channels, KCNQ2/3 potassium channels and neurofascin-186.
scenes.visual: Channels and an adhesion molecule dock onto ankyrin G: sodium channels, KCNQ2/3, neurofascin-186.
scenes.narration: Through its ANK repeats, it also binds sodium channels, KCNQ2/3 potassium channels and neurofascin-186.

scenes.tts: The initial segment has two jobs. The first is electrical.
scenes.visual: Two job cards: 1. electrical; 2. holding polarity.
scenes.narration: The initial segment has two jobs. The first is electrical.

scenes.tts: A high density of sodium channels, among other features, gives it a low threshold.
scenes.visual: Sodium channels crowd the collar; a threshold line sits low.
scenes.narration: A high density of sodium channels, among other features, gives it a low threshold.

scenes.tts: So in many neurons, this is where the action potential starts.
scenes.visual: A spike starts at the collar and travels down the gold axon.
scenes.narration: So in many neurons, this is where the action potential starts.

scenes.tts: In 1999, Bettina Winckler, Paul Forscher and Ira Mellman tested whether the membrane itself is divided there.
scenes.visual: Card 2 highlighted. On screen: Winckler, Forscher and Mellman, 1999.
scenes.narration: In 1999, Bettina Winckler, Paul Forscher and Ira Mellman tested whether the membrane itself is divided there.

scenes.tts: They attached small beads to membrane proteins, and dragged them with a laser trap.
scenes.visual: A bead on the membrane, gripped by a beam of light.
scenes.narration: They attached small beads to membrane proteins, and dragged them with a laser trap.

scenes.tts: In the cell body and dendrites the beads moved freely. At the initial segment they were held back.
scenes.visual: The bead glides along a dendrite, then stalls at the collar.
scenes.narration: In the cell body and dendrites the beads moved freely. At the initial segment they were held back.

scenes.tts: The hold depended on actin. How the barrier works is still argued.
scenes.visual: Label: depends on actin. A small note: mechanism still argued.
scenes.narration: The hold depended on actin. How the barrier works is still argued.

scenes.tts: Now test the scaffold. Lower ankyrin G after the initial segment has formed. The axon is already chosen.
scenes.visual: A knockdown symbol on ankyrin G in a fully polarized neuron.
scenes.narration: Now test the scaffold. Lower ankyrin G after the initial segment has formed. The axon is already chosen.

scenes.tts: What happens to the initial segment? And does map two, the dendrite protein, stay out of the axon?
scenes.caption: What happens to the initial segment? And does MAP2, the dendrite protein, stay out of the axon?
scenes.visual: MAP2 shown green in the dendrites, absent from the axon. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: What happens to the initial segment? And does MAP2, the dendrite protein, stay out of the axon?

scenes.tts: In 2008, Kristian Hedstrom, Yasuhiro Ogawa and Matthew Rasband did this.
scenes.visual: On screen: Hedstrom, Ogawa and Rasband, 2008.
scenes.narration: In 2008, Kristian Hedstrom, Yasuhiro Ogawa and Matthew Rasband did this.

scenes.tts: The initial segment fell apart. Map two spread into the axon.
scenes.caption: The initial segment fell apart. MAP2 spread into the axon.
scenes.visual: The collar disperses; green MAP2 creeps into the proximal axon.
scenes.narration: The initial segment fell apart. MAP2 spread into the axon.

scenes.tts: Near the cell body, the axon began to look like a dendrite, with dendritic spines.
scenes.visual: Spines bud on the proximal axon.
scenes.narration: Near the cell body, the axon began to look like a dendrite, with dendritic spines.

scenes.tts: Farther out, it kept axonal proteins.
scenes.visual: The distal axon stays gold.
scenes.narration: Farther out, it kept axonal proteins.

scenes.tts: So identity has to be actively held. Near the cell body, the initial segment holds it. Farther out, something else does, not yet identified.
scenes.visual: Two labels: proximal axon, held by the initial segment; distal axon, held by something else (not identified).
scenes.narration: So identity has to be actively held. Near the cell body, the initial segment holds it. Farther out, something else does, not yet identified.

scenes.tts: In 2008, Frank Bradke's laboratory, with Susana Gomis-Rüth and Corette Wierenga, made the mature neuron's cut.
scenes.visual: The two cut neurons from the first chapter return. On screen: Gomis-Rüth, Wierenga and Bradke, 2008. Cuts at several distances.
scenes.narration: In 2008, Frank Bradke's laboratory, with Susana Gomis-Rüth and Corette Wierenga, made the mature neuron's cut.

scenes.tts: When the stump was shorter than thirty-five micrometres, a dendrite became the axon. Longer stumps regrew.
scenes.caption: When the stump was shorter than 35 micrometres, a dendrite became the axon. Longer stumps regrew.
scenes.visual: A ruler at 35 micrometres: below it, a green dendrite turns gold; above it, the stump regrows.
scenes.narration: When the stump was shorter than 35 micrometres, a dendrite became the axon. Longer stumps regrew.

scenes.tts: The authors linked this to stable microtubules in the distal axon. They did not test the initial segment.
scenes.visual: Stable gold microtubules glow in the long stump. Note: initial segment not tested.
scenes.narration: The authors linked this to stable microtubules in the distal axon. They did not test the initial segment.

scenes.tts: So a young neuron's cut reopens the race easily.
scenes.visual: Young neuron's cut card: race reopens.
scenes.narration: So a young neuron's cut reopens the race easily.

scenes.tts: A mature neuron's cut reopens it only when almost the whole axon is removed.
scenes.visual: Mature neuron's cut card: race reopens only below 35 micrometres, in these cultures.
scenes.narration: A mature neuron's cut reopens it only when almost the whole axon is removed.

scenes.tts: One caution: this was all in a dish. In the brain, the race may be tilted or skipped.
scenes.visual: A cortical slice replaces the dish.
scenes.narration: One caution: this was all in a dish. In the brain, the race may be tilted or skipped.

scenes.tts: In the developing cortex, the trailing process of a migrating neuron often becomes its axon.
scenes.visual: A migrating neuron moves up through the slice, its trailing process turning gold behind it.
scenes.narration: In the developing cortex, the trailing process of a migrating neuron often becomes its axon.

scenes.tts: One pathway is clearly required there: the kinase L K B one, and the sad kinases it activates.
scenes.caption: One pathway is clearly required there: the kinase LKB1, and the SAD kinases it activates.
scenes.visual: Labels: LKB1, SAD-A, SAD-B.
scenes.narration: One pathway is clearly required there: the kinase LKB1, and the SAD kinases it activates.

scenes.tts: Cortical neurons lacking L K B one, or both sad kinases, fail to form axons.
scenes.caption: Cortical neurons lacking LKB1, or both SAD kinases, fail to form axons.
scenes.visual: A knockout neuron in the slice: no gold anywhere.
scenes.narration: Cortical neurons lacking LKB1, or both SAD kinases, fail to form axons.

scenes.tts: An axon is won in a race, then held. Loosen the hold, and the axon can lose features. Cut almost all of it away, and the race reopens.
scenes.visual: Closing card: won in a race, then held.
scenes.narration: An axon is won in a race, then held. Loosen the hold, and the axon can lose features. Cut almost all of it away, and the race reopens.
